Bayesian power and design analysis by simulation

Source: R/utils-scd-analysis.R
run_power_simulation.Rd

Simulation-based design analysis for multilevel SCD models. Data are generated under an assumed treatment effect, the model is refit by update() each replication (reusing one compiled Stan model), and the proportion of fits meeting the chosen posterior decision rule is the power. The same multilevel structure covers a single study (cases) and a meta-analysis of single-case data (cases nested in studies, set n_studies > 1 with between-study effect heterogeneity study_sd).

Usage

run_power_simulation(
  n_sims = 200,
  n_cases = 5,
  n_studies = 1,
  n_phase_a = 5,
  n_phase_b = 5,
  effect_sizes = c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5),
  autocorr = 0.2,
  icc = 0.2,
  study_sd = 0,
  slope_sd = 0,
  fit_autocor = TRUE,
  iter = 1000,
  chains = 2,
  design = "ab",
  family = "gaussian",
  coefficient = "level",
  decision_rule = "prob_direction",
  reversal_decision = c("all_transitions", "first_transition"),
  intervention_goal = c("increase", "decrease"),
  prob_threshold = 0.975,
  rope = 0.1,
  standardized = TRUE,
  prior = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  planning_target = c("pooled", "category"),
  studies_per_category = c(4, 4),
  common_effect = 0.5
)

Arguments

n_sims

Replications per effect magnitude. The reported Monte Carlo SE of a power estimate (mc_se) is the Agresti-Coull standard error sqrt(p'(1 - p') / (n_valid + 4)) with p' = (k + 2) / (n_valid + 4), where k counts the fired replications among the n_valid converged ones; at power 0.5 that is about 0.049 for 100, 0.035 for 200, and 0.025 for 400 valid replications.

n_cases

Cases per study; a positive integer or one integer per study.

n_studies

Studies. 1 for a single-study design; > 1 adds a study-level random effect (meta-analysis of single-case data).

n_phase_a, n_phase_b

Time points per phase; a positive integer or one integer per study.

effect_sizes

Treatment-effect magnitudes on the model link scale (log-rate ratio for count families). For a Gaussian family with standardized = TRUE the value is multiplied by the baseline (within-case) SD (a Cohen's-d-style planning grid). The element 0 yields the realized false-positive rate, except under prob_meaningful.

autocorr

Lag-1 autocorrelation of within-case residuals. Count power requires zero; serially dependent count power is unsupported.

icc

Intraclass correlation; sets the between-unit SD via tau = sigma * sqrt(icc / (1 - icc)). With n_studies > 1, tau^2 is split evenly between the study and case intercepts so the total ICC stays at icc. Count families have no residual SD, so sigma is fixed at 0.5 on the log scale (tau = 0.5 * sqrt(icc / (1 - icc))); the ICC is then a planning value on the latent log-rate scale, not the observed-count ICC, and the Poisson or negative binomial noise adds to it. Counts are generated from a baseline log-rate of log(50) with no serial dependence.

study_sd

Between-study SD of the treatment effect, on the same scale as effect_sizes (SD units for a standardized Gaussian family, link scale for count families); used when n_studies > 1. The fitted model then carries (1 + <tested terms> || study) when study_sd > 0 and (1 | study) otherwise.

slope_sd

Between-case SD of the treatment effect, adding case-level random-slope heterogeneity to the data-generating process. On the link scale for count families; in SD units for a standardized Gaussian family. Default 0 (homogeneous effect). With two or more level-2 units the fitted model always carries a correlated case random slope on the level change, (1 + phase_num | case), as the analysis formula does; when slope_sd > 0 and the tested coefficient is a trend term, an uncorrelated random slope on that term is added.

fit_autocor

Logical; add a level-1 AR(1) term over each series, ar(time, gr = case) or ar(time, gr = study:case) with studies, to the fitted model so it matches the autocorrelated errors the simulator generates. Gaussian family only (default TRUE). Its coefficient gets normal(0, 0.5), the default of the app.

iter, chains

MCMC iterations and chains.

design

One of "ab", "reversal", "multiple_baseline". A reversal design is simulated as ABAB with a common effect in every B phase (steps of +d, -d, +d at the three transitions) and coded with process_scd_phases() as the analysis codes it: time_A1 plus a cumulative level and trend step per transition (level_A1B1, level_B1A2, level_A2B2, and the matching trend_*). The fitted model carries all seven terms and, from two level-2 units on, the random effects of default_random_effects(): the onset step correlated with the case intercept, the later steps uncorrelated.

family

One of "gaussian", "poisson", "negbinomial".

coefficient

Coefficient carrying the effect and being tested: "level" (b_phase_num), "trend" (b_time_center), or "slope_change" (b_time_since_change). For a reversal design, "level" tests the level steps level_A1B1, level_B1A2, level_A2B2, "slope_change" the trend steps trend_A1B1, trend_B1A2, trend_A2B2, and "trend" the single baseline slope time_A1.

decision_rule

One of "prob_direction" (probability of direction pd >= prob_threshold), "prob_meaningful" (posterior probability of an effect at or beyond the ROPE bound in the improvement direction, P(effect >= rope), or P(effect <= -rope) for intervention_goal = "decrease", >= prob_threshold; one-sided like prob_meaningful_change), or "rope" (posterior probability inside the ROPE <= 1 - prob_threshold). These mirror the pd, prob_meaningful_change, and rope_prob quantities reported by the analysis decision summaries.

reversal_decision

Reversal designs only. "all_transitions" (default) fires only when every transition meets the decision rule in its expected direction: the A1-B1 and A2-B2 steps in the intervention goal direction and the B1-A2 withdrawal step opposite to it, so the effect is demonstrated three times. Each transition is then judged one-sided in its expected direction (prob_direction: P(oriented step > 0); prob_meaningful: P(oriented step >= rope); rope: posterior mass inside the ROPE <= 1 - prob_threshold with the posterior mean in the expected direction). "first_transition" tests only the onset step (level_A1B1 or trend_A1B1) with the single-coefficient rule.

intervention_goal

"increase" (default) or "decrease": the direction of improvement. effect_sizes, rope, and the prob_meaningful rule stay in magnitudes, positive for improvement; with "decrease" the data are generated with the negated effect and prob_meaningful uses P(effect <= -rope). prob_direction on a single coefficient stays two-sided.

prob_threshold

Posterior-probability threshold the chosen rule must meet to flag an effect. The default 0.975 corresponds, for the prob_direction rule, to a 5\ (pd >= 0.975 mirrors a two-sided alpha of 0.05); 0.95 mirrors a 10\ two-sided rate.

rope

Half-width of the region of practical equivalence, on the same scale as effect_sizes.

standardized

For a Gaussian family, multiply the magnitude by the baseline (within-case) SD (planning in SD units). Ignored for non-Gaussian families.

prior

A brms prior. Defaults to the priors the analysis uses: generate_adaptive_priors() on the template data (simulated with no effect, so the priors do not depend on effect_sizes) passed through assemble_brms_priors() (normal(0, 2.5 * outcome SD) on coefficients for Gaussian, normal(0, 2.5) on the log scale for count families, half-Student-t SD priors, lkj(2)), plus the normal(0, 0.5) AR prior truncated to the stationary region \((-1, 1)\).

seed

Optional integer. When supplied, sets the R random-number seed for the template and reseeds every replication from seed, the effect size, and the replication index, so each effect-size row is reproducible and independent of the rest of effect_sizes; the global RNG state (.Random.seed) in place before the call is restored on exit. NULL (default) draws from and advances the current RNG state.

planning_target

"pooled" tests the overall effect; "category" tests the direct category B minus A coefficient.

studies_per_category

Two study counts, each at least two, for categories A and B. Category planning sets n_studies to their sum.

common_effect

Category A effect magnitude in the intervention goal direction. Category B adds each effect_sizes magnitude. Both use the same scale as the effect grid. Category labels are study-level and allocation is fixed. Ordinal outcomes and assurance are unsupported.

Value

A data frame with one row per magnitude: effect_size, true_beta (signed effect on the coefficient scale, negative for intervention_goal = "decrease"), power (the realized false-positive rate in the effect_size = 0 row, except under prob_meaningful), mc_se (Agresti-Coull standard error of power, which stays positive when power is 0 or 1), type_s (sign-error rate against the signed true effect, conditional on the posterior-mean sign; NA under a one-sided rule, prob_meaningful or a reversal all_transitions decision that tests more than one term (coefficient = "level" or "slope_change"), since a fired replication then has the expected sign by construction; a reversal coefficient = "trend" tests one term and reports type_s) and type_m (posterior-mean exaggeration ratio among fired replications; the posterior mean is shrunk by the prior, so this is not the MLE-based Type M quantity; for a reversal design both use the onset step), power_all (the firing rate over all n_sims, counting non-converged and failed fits as non-detections: a lower bound on power, and at magnitude 0 an optimistic (low) Type I rate, since non-convergence clusters near the null), mc_se_all (Agresti-Coull standard error of power_all over n_sims), n_valid, n_nonconverged (replications that fail the simulation screen: rank-normalized Rhat >= 1.05, bulk ESS < 100, or a non-computable value on a tested coefficient, or any divergent transition; every fit uses adapt_delta = 0.99). The screen is looser than the Rhat < 1.01 boundary of the analysis diagnostics because, at the default 2 chains of 500 post-warmup draws, Rhat crosses 1.01 by noise alone in a share of well-mixed fits; the bulk ESS floor guards the looser Rhat. Non-converged replications are excluded from power and counted against power_all, with a warning naming the total, since non-convergence is more frequent at small between-case variance and near null effects, so power (and the Type I rate at magnitude 0) is conditional on convergence; neither column bounds the Type I rate from above, and a large gap between them flags that dependence, n_divergent (how many of those had a divergent transition), n_diagnostic_failed (replications excluded because sampler diagnostics are unavailable or invalid), n_fit_failed (replications whose update() errored or returned no draws for the tested coefficient), and n_sims. An error is raised when the template model (compiled once and reused by update()) fails to fit.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
run_power_simulation(n_sims = 50, n_cases = 4,
                     effect_sizes = c(0, 0.5, 1.0),
                     decision_rule = "prob_direction")
}
